prompt:
MODE: epic

Make flow reason from, and explain to, the product-manager perspective: pipeline decisions (architecture, UX, cost, content quality) must cite the PM's stated priorities, and every explanation must be actionable for a reader who has NOT read the code. Ship this as a three-feature epic with a fixed decomposition (below); do not widen or re-cut it.

WHY (settled in a prior investigation, pipeline `should-i-redesign-flow-sub`): flow already carries PM-lens prose rules (`output.lens=pm`, `references/output-style.md` "Frame every explanation impact-first for a product-lens reader", `pause-output-contract.md`) and they measurably fail to land. Diagnosis: (a) the explaining agent's context is code — a measured merged pipeline's root held ~335k chars of tool output vs ~13k chars of prose; (b) the rule is one bullet inside ~80k tokens of skill prose; (c) nothing fails when an explanation goes technical — the pause lint checks slot structure, not perspective, and the eval harness has no explanation-quality judge. Research anchors: LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning without external feedback (Huang et al., ICLR 2024); persona labels do not improve judgment (Principled Personas, EMNLP 2025; Zheng et al., EMNLP Findings 2024) but structurally independent perspectives with a forced reconciliation step do (SPP, NAACL 2024; Du et al. multi-agent debate 2023); multi-agent failures are system-design/misalignment failures (MAST, NeurIPS 2025).

DECIDED NOT TO DO (do not re-propose): a director/dev sub-agent topology redesign (root noise is solved by f6-workflow-port; sequential tool-heavy work degrades 39-70% per added coordinating agent); a passthrough "translator" sub-agent that rewrites technical output (mistranslates without the facts); a back-and-forth mediator agent (coordination tax, subagents cannot AskUserQuestion). Do not fold the `manager-agent-flow-event-driven` epic (PR #674) into this.

FEATURES (ids fixed: f1-product-brief, f2-explanation-judge, f3-product-critic):

f1-product-brief — walking-skeleton root. A standing product-brief contract at `.flow/product.md` (precedent: `.flow/design/foundation.md`, documented in `references/consumer-repo-contract.md`), with a `~/.flow/product.md` user-level fallback when the repo has none. Fields: who the PM is and what they optimize for; ranked priorities (cost/token spend, UX, content quality, reliability, ...); what "good" looks like; non-goals; vocabulary to use / avoid. Read at these sites: discovery (a required read-obligation in `discovery-instructions.md`, same shape as the committed-foundation read; Problem Statement, Decision analysis stakes, and value-prop blocks cite it); the step-3 cross-model plan review brief (`flow-plan-review`); `flow-gate-summary` / `flow-pipeline-summary` TLDR authoring; the PR body `## Why` / `## User-facing changes`. Threading via a PATH helper or jq — never a `bin/lib` import from subagent context (subagents run in consumer worktrees). Zero-cost-when-absent: with no product.md anywhere, behaviour and artifacts are byte-identical to today. Ship flow's own `.flow/product.md` (the flow repo's PM is its single user; priorities: reads outcomes not mechanisms, weighs cost/UX/content quality, never assumes the code was read).

f2-explanation-judge — depends on f1. A `flow-explain-judge` Bun helper that runs a fixed-model, fixed-effort, spend-capped check through `flow-claude-headless` (the ONLY sanctioned headless site — never a raw `claude -p`) with the rubric "could a reader who has not opened the code understand the consequence and act on this?", citing the product brief's priorities when present. Wired at the named pause sites (the step-3 plan-summary block, the AWAITING APPROVAL / GATED / MERGED / NEEDS HUMAN TLDR+WHY strings, the triaged-no-change answer) and on the PR body's Why / User-facing changes. Verdict pass / rewrite; on rewrite the supervisor rewrites ONCE and re-judges; the judge is advisory and never blocks a terminal state or changes a gate verdict. Emit telemetry via `bin/lib/telemetry.ts` `recordEvent` at the helper. Add an eval scenario to the f1-eval-harness suite that scores PM-readability of pause blocks and PR bodies with an LLM-judge rubric, runnable with `--ablation with-without`, so the delta is measured before merge and regressions are caught later.

f3-product-critic — depends on f1 and on f2's eval scenario as its no-regression gate. A structurally blind one-shot product critic at two sites, both riding EXISTING Task-tool exemptions (no eighth exemption, no nesting, artifact-mediated, one-shot): (a) step 3, after discovery writes plan.md: an agent that reads plan.md + product.md + the verbatim request and NEVER code (blindness contract modelled on `agents/core/flow-review-intent-guess.md`), writes `.flow-tmp/product-critique.md` — objections and questions in the pause-output six-slot vocabulary — and discovery's revision pass must record each point as accepted/overridden with rationale (same shape as the `### Cross-model review (AGY)` subsection); (b) step 8: a seventh review lens `agents/core/flow-review-product.md` reading the diff's user-facing surfaces, the PR body Test Steps, and product.md, gated by `flow-review-scope` (on whenever a product brief resolves), findings merged by the consolidator like the other six. Ledger updates: exemption #1's "six review agents" becomes seven in AGENTS.md, `flow-pipeline/SKILL.md`, `flow-pr-review/SKILL.md`, and the `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts` pins. Default model for the critic and lens: same as the existing lenses.

CONSTRAINTS: Bun for everything under bin/, tests next door; no new Task-tool exemption, no nested subagents, no new AskUserQuestion form; every pause message per `pause-output-contract.md`; helper-emitted telemetry only; measured via `docs/eval` (`flow-eval`), not asserted. Feature pipelines run on opus / effort high.

ASSUMPTIONS — treat as answered, do NOT fire the clarification round: scope is flow-self plus consumer repos; product.md is per-repo with the user-level fallback above; the judge's spend cap is on the order of a few cents per pause point and it is advisory-only; f2 and f3 run in parallel once f1 merges; no UI surfaces are touched, so no design foundation or browser pass applies.

features.title: Standing product-brief contract + resolver + threading
features.description: Add a standing product-brief contract to flow so pipeline decisions and explanations can cite the product manager's stated priorities. Ship `bin/flow-product-brief.ts` (Bun, `#!/usr/bin/env bun`, `chmod +x`, `import.meta.main`-gated `main()`, test next door) — a PATH helper that resolves the repo's `.flow/product.md` first, then the user-level `~/.flow/product.md` fallback, and prints one JSON line `{found, scope, path, text}`, always exiting 0 so no caller needs a guard. It is auto-shipped by `discoverHelpers` in `bin/lib/sources.ts` (every non-MAINTAINER_ONLY `bin/*.ts`); verify the symlink lands with `command -v flow-product-brief` after `flow install --upgrade`. The brief's fields, precedent-matched to `.flow/design/foundation.md`: who the PM is and what they optimize for; ranked priorities (cost/token spend, UX, content quality, reliability, ...); what "good" looks like; non-goals; vocabulary to use and avoid. Thread the resolved brief into five authoring sites: (1) `/flow-product-planning` discovery, as a required read-obligation shaped exactly like the existing "(e) Committed foundation is REQUIRED context" rule in `skills/pipeline/flow-product-planning/references/discovery-instructions.md`, with the Problem Statement, the Decision-analysis stakes lines, and the candidate value-prop blocks citing it; (2) the step-3 cross-model plan-review battery prompt, via a new optional field on `BatteryPromptInput` in `bin/lib/plan-review-prompt.ts` plus its caller `bin/flow-plan-review.ts`, pinned by `bin/lib/plan-review-prompt.test.ts`; (3) the TLDR-authoring instructions the supervisor follows before every `flow-gate-summary` / `flow-pipeline-summary` render, in `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/SKILL.md` and `references/failure-recovery.md`; (4) the PR-body `## Why` and `## User-facing changes` template in `discovery-instructions.md`. Subagent-facing sites read the brief by bare PATH name or `jq` over the resolved file — never a `bin/lib` import, since subagents run in the consumer/target worktree where flow's `bin/lib` does not exist. Zero-cost-when-absent is a hard requirement: with no `.flow/product.md` and no `~/.flow/product.md`, every threaded prompt string and rendered artifact must be byte-identical to today, proven by unit tests over each threading site's output, not by inspection. Document the contract in `references/consumer-repo-contract.md` (a `## Product brief` section next to `## Design foundation`), `AGENTS.md` `## Consumer-repo notes`, and `templates/AGENTS.md.template`. Finally, commit flow's own `.flow/product.md`: flow's PM is its single user; priorities are reading outcomes not mechanisms, weighing cost/token spend, UX and content quality, and never assuming the reader opened the code. Do not add a judge, a critic, or a review lens here — those are f2 and f3. Part of epic `make-flow-reason-from-explain` (feature `f1-product-brief`) — design at `.flow/epics/make-flow-reason-from-explain/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1+D2 — what a product brief is, where it lives, how precedence and absence resolve, and how it reaches an authoring context that cannot import bin/lib. The walking-skeleton root: one file contract, one resolver, its first readers.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a repo carries `.flow/product.md` THE SYSTEM SHALL have `flow-product-brief` print `{found: true, scope: "repo", path, text}` on one JSON line and exit 0.
WHEN a repo carries no `.flow/product.md` but `~/.flow/product.md` exists THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve the user-level file and report `scope: "user"`.
WHEN neither file exists THE SYSTEM SHALL print `{found: false}` and exit 0 — never a non-zero exit, never a thrown error.
WHEN no brief resolves THE SYSTEM SHALL leave every threading site's rendered string byte-identical to its pre-change output, asserted by a unit test per site (buildBatteryPrompt included).
WHEN a brief resolves THE SYSTEM SHALL include its ranked priorities verbatim in the cross-model plan-review battery prompt, pinned by `bin/lib/plan-review-prompt.test.ts`.

WHEN `/flow-product-planning` discovery runs with a resolved brief THE SYSTEM SHALL read it as REQUIRED context and cite it in the Problem Statement, the Decision-analysis stakes lines, and the candidate value-prop blocks.

WHEN the PR is opened THE SYSTEM SHALL carry flow's own committed `.flow/product.md` and the contract documented in `references/consumer-repo-contract.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `templates/AGENTS.md.template`.
WHEN `npm run verify` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass typecheck, vitest and lint with the new helper's colocated test suite included.

features.title: Code-blind-reader explanation judge + PM-readability eval suite
features.description: Add an external check that fails when a flow explanation is only legible to someone who read the code. Ship `bin/flow-explain-judge.ts` (Bun, test next door) — a fixed-model, fixed-effort, spend-capped judge that runs through `flow-claude-headless` (via `bin/lib/claude-headless.ts`; the only sanctioned headless site — never a raw `claude -p`, and never nested inside another headless child, which the helper's `FLOW_HEADLESS_DEPTH` guard already refuses). It takes the text to judge as `--text-file` (keep the invocation short, per the headless contract), a `--site` id naming the render site, and `--max-budget-usd`; it passes a narrow `--allowed-tools` set and an explicit `--effort`. Its rubric is "could a reader who has not opened the code understand the consequence and act on this?", and when `flow-product-brief` resolves a brief the rubric cites that brief's ranked priorities. Output is one JSON line — `{verdict: "pass"|"rewrite", reasons: [...], site, model, effort, total_cost_usd}` on success, or `{ran: false, skipReason}` on any runtime skip — always exit 0 so no caller needs a guard. Wire it at the named pause sites in `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/SKILL.md` and `references/failure-recovery.md`: the step-3 plan-summary block, the AWAITING APPROVAL / GATED / MERGED / NEEDS HUMAN TLDR and WHY strings authored before each `flow-gate-summary` render, and the `triaged-no-change` answer written via `flow-state-update --answer-stdin`; plus the PR body's `## Why` and `## User-facing changes` at PR-open time. The judge is ADVISORY: on `rewrite` the supervisor rewrites ONCE, re-judges ONCE, and then proceeds regardless of the second verdict; it never blocks a terminal state, never changes `flow-gate-decide`'s verdict, and never loops. Emit telemetry helper-side only — add `explain.judge` to `TELEMETRY_EVENTS` in `bin/lib/telemetry.ts`, call `recordEvent` inside the helper, and document the event in `docs/configuration.md`. Add a config opt-out `product.judge` (default `true`, strict `false` disables) mirroring `review.lensGates`'s shape and its `docs/configuration.md` row. Finally, add a committed eval suite `evals/pm-explanation-quality/` (suite.json plus scenarios in the shape of `evals/phase-write-fidelity/`) that scores PM-readability of pause blocks and PR bodies: the graders use the EXISTING `command` grader kind shelling out to `flow-explain-judge` over the `$ASSISTANT_TEXT` placeholder, which `gradeCommand` in `bin/lib/eval-graders.ts` already expands inside `argv` — no new grader kind is needed. The suite must run with `--ablation with-without` so the delta is recorded before merge, and `docs/eval/README.md`'s suite count and description list must be updated from four suites to five. Part of epic `make-flow-reason-from-explain` (feature `f2-explanation-judge`) — design at `.flow/epics/make-flow-reason-from-explain/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D3+D4 — what counts as an explanation a code-blind reader can act on, and how that claim is measured. Consumes f1's resolver envelope: the rubric quotes the brief's priorities when one resolves and the judge stays dormant when none does.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN `flow-explain-judge --text-file <f> --site <id>` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL emit exactly one JSON line and exit 0, whether it judged, skipped, or failed.
WHEN `claude` is missing, unauthenticated, or times out THE SYSTEM SHALL return `{ran: false, skipReason}` with the named reason and never escalate.
WHEN the judge returns `rewrite` THE SYSTEM SHALL rewrite the block once, re-judge once, and proceed regardless of the second verdict.
WHEN a terminal state or gate verdict is being rendered THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT let any judge verdict block it or alter `flow-gate-decide`'s decision, asserted by a test.
WHEN the judge is invoked from inside a `flow-claude-headless` child THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with `headless-depth-exceeded` rather than spawning.
WHEN the judge runs THE SYSTEM SHALL append one `explain.judge` event via `recordEvent` from the helper — never from agent prose.
WHEN `product.judge` is `false` in `~/.flow/config.json` THE SYSTEM SHALL skip every judge call with a named skip reason.
WHEN no product brief resolves THE SYSTEM SHALL leave every wired pause site byte-identical to today.
WHEN `bun bin/flow-eval.ts run --suite pm-explanation-quality --ablation with-without` is run THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a report carrying a per-scenario PM-readability score for both arms.
WHEN the `pm-explanation-quality` suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL include at least one known-bad fixture — a deliberately code-centric explanation — and fail the suite if the judge returns `pass` on it.
WHEN `npm run verify` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass, with the suite validated by `bin/evals-suites.test.ts` and no vitest spec spawning `claude`.

features.title: Blind plan-time product critic + seventh product review lens
features.description: Add a product perspective that is structurally blind to the code, at two sites, both riding EXISTING Task-tool exemptions — no eighth exemption, no nested subagents, no new AskUserQuestion form, artifact-mediated and one-shot. Site (a), plan time: `agents/core/flow-product-critic.md`, spawned at `/flow-pipeline` step 3 after discovery writes `plan.md`, under the existing `/flow-product-planning` Independent Discovery exemption. Its blindness contract is modelled on `agents/core/flow-review-intent-guess.md`: it reads `plan.md`, the resolved product brief, and the verbatim request, and NEVER repository code — name the off-limits surfaces explicitly the way the intent-guess definition does. It writes `.flow-tmp/product-critique.md` — objections and questions expressed in the `pause-output-contract.md` six-slot vocabulary — and discovery's revision pass must record each point as accepted or overridden with rationale, in the same shape as the existing `### Cross-model review (AGY)` subsection. Site (b), review time: `agents/core/flow-review-product.md`, a seventh `/flow-pr-review` lens under the existing Multi-Agent Review exemption, reading the diff's user-facing surfaces, the PR body's Test Steps, and the product brief, writing `.flow-tmp/agent-output-product.json` in the standard agent-finding shape. It is gated by `flow-review-scope` and runs whenever a product brief resolves; its artifact rides the OPTIONAL, tolerated-absent contract that `agent-output-gemini.json` already uses, so the consolidator's six-mandatory-artifact escalation is untouched and a repo with no brief is byte-identical to today. Ledger updates that must move atomically: the "six review agents" wording in `AGENTS.md`, `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/SKILL.md` and `skills/pipeline/flow-pr-review/SKILL.md` becomes seven; the agent-table row count pin in `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts` (`extractSkillAgentKebabs().length`) moves with it; `AGENT_LENS_MAP` in `bin/flow-pr-agent-lens.ts`, `ALL_AGENT_NAMES` and the gate rules in `bin/lib/review-lens-gates.ts`, and the agent enums in `bin/lib/agent-finding-schema.ts` all gain the `product` lens; and the consolidator's input list in `skills/pipeline/flow-pr-review/SKILL.md` Step 3.5 and `skills/pipeline/flow-consolidator-instructions/SKILL.md` names the new artifact as tolerated-absent. Both new agent definitions omit `model:` and `effort:` from frontmatter (per `AGENT_FRONTMATTER_POLICY` in `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts`), so the critic and the lens default to the same model as the existing lenses. Both spawn sites must load the Task schema via `ToolSearch query="select:Task"` before invoking Task, per the existing preamble lint. No-regression gate: leave `evals/pm-explanation-quality` green when that suite exists. Part of epic `make-flow-reason-from-explain` (feature `f3-product-critic`) — design at `.flow/epics/make-flow-reason-from-explain/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D5 — how a product perspective that never saw the code is produced and reconciled. Consumes f1's resolver envelope: it is what the critic objects from and what gates the seventh lens.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN step 3's discovery has written `plan.md` and a brief resolves THE SYSTEM SHALL spawn one blind product critic that writes `.flow-tmp/product-critique.md` in the pause-output six-slot vocabulary.

WHEN the critic runs THE SYSTEM SHALL keep it blind to repository code, with the off-limits surfaces named explicitly in `agents/core/flow-product-critic.md` the way `flow-review-intent-guess.md` names its own.
WHEN a critique exists THE SYSTEM SHALL have the plan's revision pass record every point as accepted or overridden with rationale, in the same shape as `### Cross-model review (AGY)`.
WHEN `/flow-pr-review` step 3 fans out and a brief resolves THE SYSTEM SHALL run the product lens and have the consolidator merge its findings alongside the other lenses.

WHEN the product lens reviews a diff THE SYSTEM SHALL restrict its findings to mismatches between user-visible behaviour or explanation and the brief's stated priorities, explicitly deferring code-quality, performance and security concerns to the other six lenses, with that exclusion named in `agents/core/flow-review-product.md`.
WHEN no product brief resolves THE SYSTEM SHALL skip both sites and leave step 3 and step 8 byte-identical to today.
WHEN the product lens artifact is absent THE SYSTEM SHALL tolerate it exactly as `agent-output-gemini.json`'s absence is tolerated, never raising `consolidator-missing-artifact`.

WHEN `npm run verify` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass with the lens-count pins updated in lockstep across AGENTS.md, both SKILL.md files, `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts`, `bin/flow-pr-agent-lens.ts`, `bin/lib/review-lens-gates.ts` and `bin/lib/agent-finding-schema.ts`.

WHEN the PR is opened THE SYSTEM SHALL add no new Task-tool exemption, no nested subagent, and no new AskUserQuestion form — both spawn sites ride existing exemptions and load the Task schema via ToolSearch first.
WHEN `evals/pm-explanation-quality` exists THE SYSTEM SHALL leave it green.
